cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: Polyglot persistence is using more than one type of database in the same system, each for the workload it handles best: for example PostgreSQL for orders, Redis for caching, Elasticsearch for search and a warehouse for analytics.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: Keep strongly consistent transactional data in a relational source of truth and move other workloads to specialized stores synced with change data capture or events. The cost is operational complexity and eventual consistency between stores.

questions.q: Can one transaction span PostgreSQL, Redis and Elasticsearch?
questions.a: Generally no. Use one source of truth and sync the others asynchronously via CDC or events.

questions.q: What usually stays in the relational database?
questions.a: Strongly consistent transactional data like orders and payments.

questions.q: What is the main cost of polyglot persistence?
questions.a: More operational complexity and eventual consistency between stores.
